mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes E Class 350 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only rebuilt M272 and M276 engines range from £3,200 to £6,500 depending on engine code and condition. With specialist fitting, budget £3,600-£7,300 total. M272.943 (E 280, 231 hp, 2006-2009): rebuilt £3,200-£4,800. M272.964 (E 350, 272 hp, 2004-2009): rebuilt £3,500-£5,200. M276 (E 350, 306 hp, 2011-2016): rebuilt £4,200-£6,500. Labour adds £400-£800 depending on specialist location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of balance shaft failure in an E Class 280 / 350 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cold-start rattling from the front of the engine that disappears after a few seconds is the classic early warning sign. Check engine light with cam-correlation codes (P0016, P0017) is the next stage. Rattling on cold start, fading after oil pressure builds. Check engine light with cam-correlation fault codes. Rough running on startup that smooths out within seconds. Balance shaft and timing chain replacement at a specialist costs £1,500-£2,500.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on an older E Class 350 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the car is otherwise sound. W211 E 350 petrol examples with good service history command £2,000-£5,000 used; W212 examples command £4,000-£10,000, making replacement viable. A quality rebuilt M272 costs £3,200-£5,200 supply only. W211 petrol V6 models are increasingly sought after as modern classics. A replacement engine with warranty costs less than financing a newer car. Specialist fitting adds £400-£800, not dealer rates of £1,500+.

mainEntity.name: What causes the M272 balance shaft to fail on E Class 350 petrol models?

acceptedAnswer.text: The balance shaft sprocket wears prematurely due to a design flaw in early M272 engines. This causes the timing chain to stretch and timing to drift. Balance shaft sprocket wear typically occurs between 60,000-120,000 miles. Cold-start rattling from the front of the engine is the early warning. Balance shaft and timing chain replacement at a specialist costs £1,500-£2,500. Post-2006 production engines have improved parts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M272 and M276 engines in the E Class?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 is a 90-degree V6 with a balance shaft, available in 3.0-litre (231 hp) and 3.5-litre (272 hp) forms. The M276 is a later 60-degree V6, more powerful (306 hp) and generally more reliable. M272: 90° V-angle, balance shaft required, manifold or direct injection, 231-272 hp. M276: 60° V-angle, no balance shaft, direct injection, 306 hp. M272 known for balance shaft sprocket wear; M276 known for NOx sensor issues. The M276 superseded the M272 in 2011.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes E Class 350 petrol engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance and regular oil changes, M272 and M276 engines regularly reach 200,000-300,000 miles. The M276 timing components may require attention around 250,000 km. M272/M276 V6 bottom ends are robust when properly maintained. Balance shaft inspection/replacement at 60k-120k miles is recommended for early M272. Regular oil changes (8,000 miles) are critical for timing chain and phaser life. The M276 is generally more reliable than the M272.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz E Class 280 / 350 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The E 280 and E 350 petrol badges represented Mercedes-Benz's V6 petrol offerings across the W211 and W212 E-Class generations. The E 280 used the M272 3.0-litre V6, while the E 350 was powered by larger M272 3.5-litre V6 - and later the M276 3.5-litre V6 in the W212. The M272 engine family was introduced in 2004 to replace the M112 V6, featuring a 90-degree V-angle with a balance shaft, double overhead camshafts per bank, and four valves per cylinder. The M276 superseded the M272 in 2011.

milestones.description: **2004** - W211 E 350 launched with M272.964 3.5-litre V6, 200 kW (272 hp), 350 Nm
**2006** - W211 E 280 launched with M272.943 3.0-litre V6, 170 kW (231 hp), 300 Nm
**2006** - M272 direct injection (CGI) introduced in some markets from 2007 onwards
**2009** - W212 generation launched; E 350 continues with M272.961 engine
**2011** - M276 engine supersedes M272 in E-Class range

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes E Class 280 / 350 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The M272 V6 engine that powers the majority of E Class 280 and 350 petrol models is a refined, smooth powerplant - but the infamous balance shaft sprocket wear has become the defining repair of this engine family. The later M276 is more reliable but introduces its own set of issues around NOx sensors and timing components. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down what these failures cost to fix and when replacement is the smarter option.

problems.h4: Balance Shaft Sprocket Wear - The M272 Achilles Heel in the E Class 280 / 350 Petrol
problems.rootCause: The M272 V6 uses a balance shaft between the cylinder banks to reduce first and second order inertial forces. The balance shaft sprocket wears prematurely on early M272 engines. This causes timing chain stretch and camshaft correlation faults (P0016/P0017 codes). Cold-start rattling from the front of the engine is the classic early warning sign. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, bending valves and destroying the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of balance shaft sprocket, timing chain, tensioner and guides - front of engine removal required
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-120,000 miles; effective if caught before chain jumps

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chain replacement plus camshaft adjuster/phaser replacement
repairOptions.longevity: When phaser wear is also present; phasers wear independently of chain

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt M272 with upgraded balance shaft and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has jumped causing valvetrain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W211 E 350 petrol is worth £2,000-£5,000 depending on condition and mileage; a W212 E 350 commands £4,000-£10,000【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. If the vehicle is worth under £3,000, a used engine may be the pragmatic choice. For W211 cars worth £3,500+ and W212 cars worth £5,000+, a rebuilt engine with warranty can be justified if the rest of the car is sound.
problems.recommendation: The cold-start rattle is your early warning - don't ignore it. The balance shaft sprocket issue is a known design weakness on early M272 engines. A specialist balance shaft and timing chain replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is significantly cheaper than the £4,000+ engine replacement if the chain jumps. If you own an early W211 E 350, this is preventative maintenance worth budgeting for - many owners have been caught out by this failure. The issue was addressed on later M272 engines (post-2006 production).
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M272 Mercedes E Class 280 / 350 petrol engine prices

problems.h4: Camshaft Adjuster (Phaser) Failure - The M272 and M276 Top-End Issue
problems.rootCause: Cam phasers on the M272 and M276 engine families are oil-pressure-actuated variable-valve-timing actuators that wear independently of the timing chain. A worn or stuck phaser produces cam-correlation faults before the chain itself stretches enough to cause its own codes. On the M276, camshaft adjuster and cam follower wear is reported. Oil pressure issues can mimic phaser failure, so proper diagnosis is essential.

Replacement of phasers, timing chain, tensioner and guides together
repairOptions.longevity: When both phaser and chain wear are present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt engine with new phasers and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: When phaser failure has caused valvetrain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W211 £2,000-£5,000; W212 £4,000-£10,000). On a car worth over £4,000, £1,200-£2,000 for phaser replacement is a manageable expense to protect a valuable asset.
problems.recommendation: Cam phaser issues can be difficult to distinguish from timing chain problems without proper diagnostics. If you have cam-correlation codes (P0016, P0017) combined with cold-start rattle, a specialist diagnosis using live ECU data is essential. On the M276, phaser and follower issues are less common than on the M272, but still reported. Regular oil changes with the correct specification oil are critical - these components are oil-pressure-actuated.

problems.h4: M276 NOx Sensor Failure & Oil Leaks - The Later V6 Weaknesses
problems.rootCause: Original factory NOx sensors on the M276 are known to fail after 2-3 years. Replacement sensors were on backorder during COVID, and a new version was released after several years. Oil leaks from timing cover gaskets and camshaft adjusters are reported. The M276 is generally considered more reliable than the M272, but these issues still affect many examples.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of faulty NOx sensors, typically both banks
repairOptions.longevity: 20,000-50,000 miles; original sensors are known to fail

repairOptions.longevity: When oil loss has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W212 E 350 petrol is worth £4,000-£10,000【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. At these values, £250-£500 for NOx sensor replacement is a minor expense to keep the car running correctly.
problems.recommendation: NOx sensor failure on the M276 is frustrating but rarely requires engine replacement - the most cost-effective approach is replacement with the updated sensor version. For oil leaks, early diagnosis is key - timing cover gasket leaks can worsen over time and may indicate timing component wear. Regular oil changes with the correct specification oil are essential for M276 longevity.
